argv:
Rewrite the text following the principles of Simplified Technical English.

Use one topic per sentence. Keep procedural sentences to twenty words or
fewer and descriptive sentences to twenty-five words or fewer. Keep paragraphs
to six sentences or fewer.

Use the active voice. Address the reader directly with the imperative for
instructions. Use only the simple present, simple past, and simple future
tense.

Use one word for one meaning throughout, and one meaning for one word: never
vary a term for elegance. Prefer short, common words over long or technical
ones. Do not use noun clusters of more than three words. Write out what a
pronoun refers to whenever there is any doubt.

Do not use slang, idioms, or metaphors.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, and dependent on each other in so complex a manner, have all been produced by laws acting around us. These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. Thus, from the war of nature, from famine and death, the most exalted object which we are capable of conceiving, namely, the production of the higher animals, directly follows. There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
</passage>

response.text:
Think about a tangled bank of plants. Many kinds of plants grow there. Birds sing in the bushes. Insects fly around. Worms move through the wet soil.

These living things have complex shapes. Each shape differs from the others. Each living thing depends on other living things in complex ways. Natural laws around us produced all these living things.

Several laws work together. First, living things grow and reproduce. Second, living things inherit traits from their parents. This inheritance happens because of reproduction. Third, living things vary. External conditions cause this variation. Use and disuse of body parts also cause this variation.

Living things reproduce at a high rate. This high rate causes a struggle for life. The struggle for life causes natural selection. Natural selection causes character divergence. Natural selection causes less-improved forms to become extinct.

Nature fights a constant war. Famine and death occur often. From this war, famine, and death, one great result follows: the production of higher animals. We can imagine no more important result than this.

This view of life shows grandeur. A few forms of life started with these natural powers. Perhaps only one form of life started this way. Earth has followed the fixed law of gravity through many cycles. From this simple beginning, endless forms have evolved. These forms show great beauty. These forms show great wonder. These forms continue to evolve today.
